artboards.name: home-page
artboards.role: Forno Rosso pizzeria marketing home page: site header/nav shell, hero, delivery-promise banner, featured-menu grid, brand-story section, and footer. The linked node is a single FRAME (not a CANVAS of several artboards), so the whole page is one screen; there is only one artboard to review. The current story's scope is the header/navigation shell (row 1), the rest of the page is mapped for completeness and context.

open_questions.topic: Header/nav shell has no mobile or tablet breakpoint
open_questions.detail: The Figma frame is fixed at 1440px wide (desktop only). No hamburger/drawer menu, collapsed nav state, or narrower header layout is drawn anywhere in the source frame, even though this story is specifically about the site header & navigation shell. Implementing a mobile nav pattern now would mean inventing UI that is not in the source of truth.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement SiteHeader/PrimaryNav exactly as designed for the ≥1440px desktop breakpoint only. Do not invent a hamburger/drawer pattern; treat small-viewport header behavior as out of scope until a mobile design is supplied.

options.label: Build only the desktop header now; request a follow-up design for mobile/tablet nav before implementing it
Invent a conventional hamburger/drawer pattern now, using generic best practice not present in the Figma frame

open_questions.topic: Delivery time shown twice with different values
open_questions.detail: Header shows 'Estimated delivery: 30 mins' (node 6:21) while the delivery banner below states 'Average ETA: 25 - 35 Min' (node 6:50). These may be intentional (a live order estimate vs. a general site-wide average) or simply inconsistent placeholder copy.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement both strings literally as authored, as two independent copy sources (no shared data binding), and flag the discrepancy for content review.

open_questions.topic: Whether the header should be sticky/fixed on scroll
open_questions.detail: Every node in the frame, including the header, carries Figma's default 'SCROLLS' scroll behavior rather than 'STICKY_SCROLLS', meaning the design does not specify a pinned header.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement SiteHeader in normal document flow (non-sticky), matching the frame's scrollBehavior; do not add position:sticky/fixed since that would be an invented behavior.

open_questions.detail: PrimaryNav includes a plain 'Cart' text link (node 6:19) alongside a separate icon+badge CartButton (node 6:22) in the same header row.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Keep both as designed and map them to two distinct components (NavLink and CartButton) rather than merging them; the nav link likely routes to a full cart page while the icon button is a quick-access affordance with a live item count.

open_questions.topic: Whether hero CTAs and card 'Add to Order' buttons share one Button component
open_questions.detail: Hero has a primary red-fill button with a trailing arrow icon and an outline button with no icon; each MenuItemCard has a dark-fill button with a leading plus icon. All three share size, radius (8px), and type style but differ in fill/border/icon placement.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Model all three as a single shared Button component with variant ('primary' | 'outline' | 'dark') and icon/iconPosition props, instead of three near-duplicate components.

open_questions.topic: Whether featured-section and story-section headings share one SectionHeading component
open_questions.detail: featured-section uses a brand-red uppercase eyebrow with a short rule under the title; story-section uses a brand-green uppercase eyebrow with no rule. Layout (eyebrow above serif title) is otherwise identical.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Model both as a single shared SectionHeading component with eyebrowTone ('accent' | 'brand') and showRule props, instead of two separate components.

open_questions.topic: Rest of the page (4-col menu grid, 2-col hero/story) has no responsive design either
open_questions.detail: Beyond the header, FeaturedGrid (4 columns) and the hero/story two-column layouts are only specified at 1440px. This is outside the current story's scope but noted for the team building the rest of the page.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Out of scope for this story; implement the header/nav shell at the designed breakpoint only, and leave responsive treatment of the remaining sections to whichever story implements them.
